llm_summary_material: **Black holes** — Treat Hawking-radiation evaporation as operationally irrelevant: a solar-mass hole needs ~10⁶⁷ years to evaporate, far beyond any planning horizon.

**Coffee processing** — Process cherries within hours of picking and choose the method deliberately: washed (12–72 h fermentation) for acidity/floral clarity, natural (2–4 weeks drying) for fruity profiles but only with even drying, honey as the in-between graded by residual mucilage.
**EV charging** — Match deployment to the region's plug standard (CCS in EU/NA, GB/T in China, CHAdeMO in Japan) and note that the headline "200 km in ~15 min" applies only to 800 V architectures.

**Battery economics** — Model EV costs at current cell prices (<$140/kWh in 2023, down from ~$1,100/kWh in 2010), not historical figures, and plan for solid-state as a 2027+ option rather than a present one.
**Protocol migration** — Schedule a hard cutover date: internet growth hinged on flag day (TCP/IP, 1 Jan 1983) and on replacing ad-hoc mechanisms (hosts file → DNS) with a scalable system.

**Photosynthesis benchmarks** — Compare efficiencies only under matched conditions: field crops convert ~3% of light, C4 plants (maize, sugarcane) win in hot climates, and artificial solar-to-fuel reached ~10% in 2022.
**Solar siting** — PV at ~$0.048/kWh is the cheapest new-build option in most markets, but specify CSP with molten-salt storage when electricity must be delivered after sunset.

**Wind siting** — Tier-one decision is location, because yield scales with the *cube* of wind speed; validate estimates against the Betz limit (59.3%), real-world efficiency (45–50%), and cut-in/cut-out speeds (3/25 m/s).
